title: A Scalable, Efficient, and Robust Dynamic Memory Management Library for HLS-based FPGAs
problem: HLS tools lack dynamic memory management support, forcing static memory allocation and suboptimal resource utilization. Existing DMM solutions fail to concurrently achieve scalability (managing arbitrary memory sizes), efficiency (minimal allocation latency), and robustness (low allocation failure rates).
motivation: Dynamic memory management is critical for FPGA-based architecture prototyping to enhance productivity and enable efficient resource utilization on memory-constrained hardware.
method: GraDMM solves the memory allocation problem by treating it as a graph problem—like finding paths through connected blocks of memory—and using the FPGA's specialized graph-processing hardware to solve it fast. It uses a minimal pipeline design that doesn't require extra hardware resources as memory sizes grow. To find free memory faster, it searches multiple paths at once (concurrent traversal) and uses shortcuts to jump to promising locations. Finally, it incorporates an adaptive defragmenter that reorganizes memory to prevent fragmentation from causing allocation failures.
key_novelty: The core idea is treating dynamic memory management as a graph-solving problem and using FPGA hardware specialized for graphs so that it can simultaneously achieve all three goals: scaling to large memory sizes, answering allocation requests quickly, and preventing allocation failures.
contributions: GraDMM library achieving scalability by specializing a simplified pipeline that suppresses resource utilization expansion for arbitrarily sized memory management
Data-centric concurrent traversal and shortcut-assisted fast traversal policies reducing allocation/deallocation latency by 78.94%-99.99%
Adaptive memory defragmenter minimizing fragmentation-induced allocation failures by 10.71%-65.75%
Resource consumption savings of 56.71%-85.59% compared to state-of-the-art solutions
primary_theme: Dynamic memory management for HLS-based FPGAs
